mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the risk-free rate used in equity valuation models, leading to higher present values of future cash flows and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and trigger negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Joint deterioration in housing activity (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a severe weakening of consumer demand, leading to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when the joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth (INDPRO) exceeds 0.5% monthly, it signals robust economic activity that supports corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is inactive during low growth regimes (INDPRO <= 0.5%).
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO > 0.5%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the average return in high growth regimes is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the correlation between UNRATE level and 5-day returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a deepening economic contraction, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases, or the interaction effect is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of near-zero interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), the market is in a liquidity trap where conventional monetary policy is ineffective, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate prolonged economic stagnation.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
